Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
# Bug report: back-to-back ad breaks get the wrong producer break id

A partner running channels with back-to-back ad breaks — one break ending at the exact instant the
next one begins, with no regular programming in between — is seeing broken per-break
reconciliation, but only on those specific breaks. Isolated breaks (anything with even a few
seconds of ordinary content before or after) reconcile correctly every time.

What they're seeing: when two breaks are scheduled with zero gap between them, the *second*
break's delivery data sometimes gets attributed to the *first* break's producer id instead of its
own. The dashboard shows impressions/fill against the wrong break, and the break that actually ran
shows no delivery data at all — as if it were never signalled.

They've confirmed the origin is emitting cue markers correctly for both breaks (checked directly
against the origin's own logs) — the fault isn't upstream of us.

Find and fix the defect. Do not weaken support for any marker syntax already handled today. When
you believe the fix is correct, restart whichever service needs it so the running system reflects
your change.

Do not modify the test suite, CI configuration, or any files outside this service's application
source. Your fix should be minimal and targeted at the actual defect.

steps.message:
Analysis: The detector caches every DATERANGE ID in a segment tag block and uses the first ID attached to an avail. A closing DATERANGE can therefore seed the next CUE-OUT with the previous break's ID when no segment separates the breaks. I need to inspect marker attributes before choosing the smallest fix that preserves existing syntax support.
Plan: Read the parser and remaining detector code, plus startup dependencies. Determine how to distinguish closing DATERANGE updates from opening markers without narrowing existing opening-marker support.

arguments.keystrokes: cat packages/core/src/scte.ts; sed -n '115,190p' packages/data-plane/src/avails.ts
cat packages/core/src/scte.test.ts; cat packages/storage/src/factory.ts; cat packages/persistence/src/db.ts; env | sort

steps.message:
Analysis: The defect is in data-plane avail detection: a closing SCTE35-IN DATERANGE is treated as a candidate opening ID. At a zero-gap boundary, the next CUE-OUT inherits it, and the real opening DATERANGE cannot replace it. Clearing state only at CUE-IN would not fix closing DATERANGEs emitted after CUE-IN. The fix should exclude closing-only SCTE35-IN updates from ID association, while retaining generic DATERANGEs, both marker orderings, and combined OUT/IN markers.
Plan: First reproduce the incorrect attribution using an inline assertion-free probe. Then add a targeted closing-only check in avails.ts; parse attribute names without mistaking text inside quoted values for attributes. No test or configuration files will be modified.

Analysis: The probe reproduced the bug exactly: both breaks were assigned 'first'. The targeted change now ignores SCTE35-IN-only DATERANGEs for producer-ID association, without changing the shared parser or requiring SCTE35-OUT on previously supported generic markers.
Plan: Validate adjacent breaks across closing/opening marker orderings, missing IDs, generic markers, mixed-case attributes, and combined OUT/IN syntax using in-memory assertions. Run the existing core and data-plane tests, then start the data-plane directly from updated TypeScript so no generated files need modification.
